title: Realtime publication broadcasts full public.bookings rows to any authorized subscriber
description: Migration 0001 line 112 adds public.bookings to the supabase_realtime publication. The published payload is the row image, including customer_name, customer_email, customer_phone, payment fields and cancel_token. The intended reader of bookings is only the owning business (owner_bookings, 0001:95) while anon SELECT is denied (anon_read_own_booking using (false), 0001:108). If the deployed Realtime service delivers postgres_changes without enforcing subscriber RLS, any visitor subscribing with the bundled anon key receives every tenant's booking rows as they change.
root_cause: A PII-bearing table was added to a broadcast channel that inherits none of the table-level anon denial by construction; delivery depends entirely on platform-side RLS enforcement for postgres_changes, which is not configured or constrained anywhere in the target.
intended_behavior: Only sessions whose role passes public.bookings SELECT policies should receive realtime events for that table, or the publication should expose a sanitized projection.

trace.description: alter publication supabase_realtime add table public.bookings - full row images enter the broadcast channel
anon_read_own_booking using (false) denies REST reads; whether it also filters realtime delivery is the platform-side fact under validation
project_id is the only key in config.toml; no realtime authorization setting is source-visible in the target

evidence.description: bookings is in the realtime publication
customer_name/customer_email/customer_phone columns exist on the broadcast row
cancel_token column exists on the broadcast row
anon REST select is denied, so any realtime leak is a channel that bypasses that control

conditions.description: The deployed Supabase Realtime must deliver postgres_changes without enforcing the subscriber's RLS, or the subscriber must hold a role whose SELECT policy on bookings passes.
Supabase Realtime version/platform behavior for postgres_changes RLS enforcement is not determinable from the target source.

execution.attacker_perspective: An anonymous visitor subscribes to postgres_changes on public.bookings using the anon key bundled in the built app and observes whether events arrive.
instructions: In a browser console on the deployed app, run the payload with the existing window client.
Create or update one booking from a second browser session (a test booking against a dummy tenant).
Observe whether any event payload containing customer PII or cancel_token arrives.
execution.observed_result: Not executed in this run: target-controlled execution is prohibited on this host (no OS-enforced sandbox) and the decisive fact is the deployed Realtime platform behavior. Source evidence is complete; the behavioral check is the validation plan.

remediation.strategy: Do not broadcast raw booking rows. Either remove bookings from the realtime publication and expose a sanitized view (like booked_slots) to the publication, or verify in the Supabase dashboard that Realtime enforces subscriber RLS for postgres_changes on this project before relying on the anon denial.

likelihood.reason: The publication membership is certain; delivery to anon depends on platform RLS enforcement that the run could not verify, and no in-target code subscribes to bookings today.

impact.reason: If delivered, every tenant's customer PII and cancel tokens stream to any anonymous subscriber - cross-tenant PII disclosure with real consequences.

confidence.reason: Source evidence is exact and unambiguous; only the platform delivery behavior remains open, which is why the record is needs_validation rather than confirmed.
